transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-06 16:00 PDT | Duration ~62m | Recording: Fireflies auto | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Miguel (Redwood CSM), Janelle (Stratify Head of ML), Marcus (Platform), Tara (Security), Deepak (SRE)

Summary: Short sync to align on cutover orchestration for the pilot -> production flip. Focused on canary thresholds, what metrics will gate traffic, and who owns rollback steps. Some audio glitches halfway; occasional mislabels.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — runbook review, canary metrics, telemetry, and dry-run schedule.
[00:18] Janelle (Stratify): yep thanks alex, running a bit late here in SF but we have the platform folks. main ask is minimize risk to patient-facing endpoints — low latency needs.
[00:32] Priya (Redwood): cool. quick callout: we'll propose two canary phases — 1% initial traffic for smoke, then 10% progressive shift with metric gating. we'll describe exact alerts that auto-fail the shift.
[00:48] Marcus (Stratify): 1% sounds reasonable, what SLA are you targeting for p50/p95? our internal SLO is p95 < 220ms for inference.
[01:05] Priya: in our hosted benchmark with quantized model variant we see p95 around 170-200ms depending on payload; for private we add network overhead so plan for 200-260ms. measurement will be end-to-end including VPC egress.
[01:28] Tara (Stratify): we need to capture e2e latency and also per-route token billing spikes — security wants to see audit trails and KMS wrapped keys for any customer data. is KMS rotation handled in the private deployment?
[01:48] Alex: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations; we'll include key rotation docs in the runbook. Miguel will link the security checklist.
[02:03] Miguel (Redwood): linking the checklist now — note: some of the field names in that doc were auto-linted, apologies for stray typos.
[02:18] Deepak (Stratify): network windows — we can carve a maintenance window Thurs 02:00-04:00 PDT for VPC peering, if that's acceptable.
[02:32] Marcus: we can do that but prefer nights if possible. also need to confirm egress IPs so firewall rules can be preloaded.
[02:46] Priya: we'll provide the IP ranges. next, on canary gating, propose the gating metric set: error rate, p95 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and model perplexity or quality regression score.
[03:05] Janelle: quality regression — we need to verify how you compute that. our test prompts are medical triage-like — will the model hallucinate?
[03:20] Priya: good point. SE note: we'll run a prompt set baseline; measure rouge-ish metrics + custom heuristics. fairness caveat: automatic metrics can miss clinical hallucinations, so we'll lock human review as part of the 10% stage.
[03:42] Alex: also plan for automatic rollback if error rate > 0.5% or latency p95 degrades by 30% vs baseline. open to adjust.
[03:55] Tara: 0.5% seems tight for mis-typed patient IDs, can we instead have a composite trigger including manual gating for certain endpoints?
[04:10] Priya: yes, we can add manual holdpoints for high-risk routes. we'll mark those in the runbook.
[04:25] Marcus: how do you handle cache warmup — KV cache is important for us, we don't want cold starts during canary.
[04:38] Priya: we support prefix warming; we'll include a golden replay utility to pre-populate KV cache. planning to run the replay prior to shifting traffic.
[04:55] Deepak: replay script — can it be run from our network to avoid cross-region variance?
[05:08] Priya: yes, we'll provide a containerized runner. it needs API creds with limited scope.
[05:20] Alex: action item: priya to share replay container image + run instructions.
[05:34] Janelle: on observability — what dashboards do you suggest? we want token-level cost breakdown and model-level tracing.
[05:47] Miguel: Redwood Console has per-route token counters, model cost estimates, and a trace hook for request IDs. we'll include dashboard templates in the runbook.
[06:02] Janelle: perfect. can we get alerts routed to pagerduty?
[06:10] Miguel: yes - PD integration is standard. we'll map severity levels to PD escalation.
[06:18] Tara: compliance question — how long do logs live? we may need 1 year for audit.
[06:25] Alex: retention is configurable; enterprise plans can keep up to 1 year or more. we'll note retention settings in docs.
[06:38] Marcus: A/B vs canary — we prefer canary because of stateful caches, but curious if Redwood supports weighted A/B for feature flagging.
[06:52] Priya: we support both. weighted A/B is available but it's less cache-friendly; for caching heavy workloads canary or traffic mirroring with shadowing is better.
[07:07] Janelle: what about fallback model variants — e.g., small quantized backup to reduce cost and keep latency?
[07:19] Priya: yes, plan is to have an LLM-lite variant as fallback. routing policy will prefer primary model unless a metric breach triggers failover to the variant.
[07:34] Deepak: do you support graceful degradation — e.g., partial completions or shorter sequence limits?
[07:40] Priya: yes, we can reduce max tokens and change sampling to reduce latency. that's in the runbook's escalation section.
[07:52] Marcus: let's discuss the dry-run timeline. we propose: week 1 runbook review, week 2 dry-run with synthetic traffic, week 3 limited live canary, week 4 ramp. is that realistic?
[08:07] Alex: sounds reasonable. proposed dry-run date: 2025-10-15 for synthetic replay; full canary start 2025-10-20 if all green.
[08:20] Janelle: we need product ops sign-off and legal to clear the data handling. can legal give provisional sign-off by 2025-10-17?
[08:30] Tara: legal can review but security will need to confirm data classification for prompts; some prompts contain PHI, which changes routing requirements.
[08:45] Priya: for PHI we recommend private deployment in your VPC; it avoids leaving the controlled network.
[08:54] Marcus: we're aiming for private deployment for those routes and hosted for low-sensitivity ones. how does Redwood handle mixed routing?
[09:08] Alex: policy-based routing is supported — route by tag or endpoint; we'll include policy examples.
[09:18] Deepak: what about scaling? during spikes we can't afford request queuing that blows past SLA. how fast do dedicated pools scale?
[09:30] Priya: autoscaling is fast for short bursts but there's an instance spin-up time; we recommend burst capacity reservations and pre-warming when we see predictable schedules.
[09:44] Marcus: note - we have weekly batch jobs that spike qps at ~03:00 UTC each night.
[09:50] Alex: we'll factor that into capacity planning.
[10:00] Miguel: small note — a previous doc had 'KV cash' typo instead of 'KV cache', just flagging potential transcription errors in shared notes.
[10:12] Janelle: ha, yes.
[10:18] Priya: on metrics gating specifics: propose thresholds: error rate < 0.2% during canary, p95 latency within +20% of baseline, model quality delta less than 0.5 on internal score. manual hold for PHI endpoints. open to adjust.
[10:39] Tara: we'll need to see the scoring function. also want SIEM integration for audit logs — can you forward syslog events?
[10:52] Alex: yes we have syslog/forwarding and S3 log delivery options. we'll include example config.
[11:02] Marcus: how are secrets managed for the replay runner?
[11:07] Priya: runner reads creds from an ephemeral token; recommend using short-lived role-based tokens.
[11:16] Janelle: question on test coverage — do you support per-prompt tag evaluation so we can quickly revert on specific prompt families?
[11:29] Priya: yes, tagging is supported — you can define prompt sets and baseline per set. the console will show regressions per-tag.
[11:40] Alex: good. any blockers on scheduling the dry-run?
[11:45] Marcus: we need to align legal and product ops; tentatively green if runbook addresses PHI routing.
[11:54] Priya: I'll incorporate PHI holdpoints and highlight them.
[12:05] (background cross talk)
[12:21] Miguel: side note - sending link to cost model sheet in chat, it's editable.
[12:30] Janelle: got it.
[12:36] Priya: let's walk the actual cutover flow quickly: pre-cutover (replay + cache warm), stage 1 1% smoke (10m hold), evaluate metrics + manual QA, stage 2 progressive shift to 10% (30m holding windows with automated gating), then 50% and 100% ramp if green.
[13:06] Deepak: how do you rollback if issues at 10%? instant cut or gradual?
[13:12] Priya: we support both. recommended: instant rollback to previous stable for critical breaches; for soft regressions we throttle back to previous percentage and run mitigation.
[13:27] Marcus: what about DB or downstream pressure — do you have safety valves to limit requests per downstream?
[13:36] Alex: will include rate limiting snippets and circuit-breaker configs in the runbook.
[13:46] Janelle: ok re: acceptance criteria — define green as all gating metrics within thresholds for two consecutive holds and manual QA pass.
[13:58] Priya: agreed. we'll capture exact numbers in the runbook.
[14:12] Alex: next, who owns the actual traffic shift? AE/SE or your ops?
[14:20] Marcus: platform ops will execute the shift; we'd like Redwood to have an operator role or a runbook with scripted ops commands.
[14:31] Priya: we'll provide a runbook with CLI/manual steps; can also run the traffic shift via API if you want automation.
[14:41] Janelle: prefer automation but with manual confirmation for PHI routes.
[14:48] Miguel: noted.
[14:55] Tara: about encryption in transit: TLS mutual auth for VPC peering is needed?
[15:02] Alex: mTLS supported for private deployments; we can include cert rotation guidance.
[15:12] Marcus: last item - reporting. we'll need a post-cutover report template with metrics, incidents, and cost delta.
[15:22] Alex: Redwood will provide a post-mortem and cost delta doc. Miguel will own the template.
[15:30] Miguel: will assign template owner and circulate.
[15:36] Priya: ok quick recap of deliverables — runbook draft, replay runner, canary metric doc, dashboard templates, IP ranges, legal/security checklist.
[15:46] Janelle: agreed. can we also get an SLA addendum template?
[15:51] Alex: yes, legal can share a template.
[15:56] (brief pause)
[16:05] Deepak: one more question — if model rollback happens, are in-flight requests failed or served by fallback?
[16:12] Priya: behavior depends on routing config: you can either fail fast or route to fallback variant. default is fail fast to avoid inconsistent outputs.
[16:22] Marcus: prefer fallback for customer UX on non-critical routes.
[16:28] Priya: we'll mark per-route policy in the runbook.
[16:36] Alex: ok time check — we're at about 16 minutes in, still lots to cover, but good progress.
[16:44] (audio blip)
[17:05] Priya: pulling up draft runbook on screen share (link posted in chat): runbook sections: prerequisites, pre-cutover checklist, canary flow, metrics gating, rollback, post-cutover report.
[17:28] Janelle: looks solid, can you make PHI-specific steps bold?
[17:34] Priya: yes will annotate.
[17:42] Marcus: can you add a checklist for firewall and IP allowlist with exact CIDR examples?
[17:50] Alex: will include.
[17:58] Tara: anything about log integrity and WORM storage for audit?
[18:04] Miguel: we can push logs to S3 with object lock for WORM compliance if needed.
[18:12] Tara: good — note for legal review.
[18:20] Janelle: ok one last structural ask — include a backout communications plan: who messages customers, internal comms, and monitoring channels.
[18:32] Alex: included. good idea.
[18:40] Priya: final note: we'll run a small smoke test during the dry-run and leave a 15m stabilization period.
[18:50] Marcus: that's helpful.
[19:00] Alex: wrap — recap of next steps in chat and action items assigned. thanks everyone.

Appendix: Links shared in chat (short notes) - Runbook draft: /redwood/runbooks/stratify-cutover-v1 (editable), Cost model sheet: /sheets/stratify-cost-model, Canary metrics spreadsheet: /sheets/stratify-canary-metrics

End of transcript. Note: transcription includes occasional mis-typed acronyms and filler words; speaker labels may be approximate.
